column1: # tests/o1/corpus/arena_idle.tsv -- the distinct state payloads of the only capture on this machine.
# Extracted from freshcap/arena_decoded.txt (a private capture), the full decode of
# freshcap/arena.bin (5,016,771 B, 34,791 datagrams, 125.387 s, 2026-05-30). Real bytes the retail PC
# engine put on the wire; this repository cannot fabricate them.
# COVERAGE IS STATED IN DISTINCT PAYLOADS, NOT RECORD COUNTS. The capture is idle:
# 5,520 PlayerState records carry ONE distinct payload and 11,029 SimState records carry SIXTEEN.
# Seventeen payloads is the coverage. No compression ratio is published from this data -- idle data
# compresses at a ratio that measures the corpus, not the codec.
# ★ THE WHOLE BODY IS STORED, AND THE RECORD START IS A COLUMN RATHER THAN AN ASSUMPTION.
# The first version of this file stored a pre-stripped tail with a 16-byte message header removed. That
# header length was checked against PlayerState and then applied unchanged to SimState, whose header is
# 24 bytes -- so the SimState decode began 64 bits early, read the framing word 0x50 as the record's
# 11-bit `bits` field, and produced an angular velocity of 367 rad/s against a field that stops at 144.
# W1-A read that refusal as evidence that the symbol was not SimState. It was evidence that the harness
# held a constant nobody had tested. Storing the header keeps it auditable and puts the offset where a
# check can fail on it.
# ★ HOW EACH OFFSET WAS PINNED, AND WHAT THE CORPUS COULD NOT SETTLE.
# An offset is accepted only if the whole record re-encodes to the identical bits AND every remaining bit
# of the body is zero padding. That leaves three candidates per symbol, not one: 128/129/140 for
# PlayerState and 192/193/214 for SimState. All three survive all 5,520 records -- which is worth exactly
# ONE payload, because the capture is idle, and is the same record-count-for-coverage error this file
# exists to avoid. The tie is broken by byte alignment: the container delivers whole-byte bodies, so a
# record starting mid-byte is not a shape anything here supports. A capture with motion collapses it for
# free; until then the alternates are named above rather than hidden.
# Both record lengths agree with the design and with W1-A's decompilation of the PC serialisers:
# PlayerState 370 bits (SR15NetPlayerState::BitPack, 0x140CB09E0), SimState 284 bits
# (SR15NetPhysicsSimState::BitPack, 0x140C515F0). Three derivations, one number each.
